title: Enhancing the phase sensitivity of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer beyond the Heisenberg limit through dynamic squeezing
authors: Lakshya Bhardwaj, Ankit Tiwari, Mohan Sarovar, Christian Arenz
abstract: We propose a method to enhance the phase sensitivity of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer, independent of its input states. This is achieved by applying squeezing sequences to one arm of the interferometer. By alternating between squeezing along orthogonal quadratures, we demonstrate that the phase sensitivity of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer can be generically enhanced. Since this enhancement is independent of the input states, the proposed dynamic squeezing method allows for further improvement in phase sensitivity when combined with non-classical input states. We compare the dynamic squeezing approach with existing quantum sensing protocols and show that super-Heisenberg scaling can be achieved. Finally, we demonstrate that the scheme is robust against moderate photon loss.
summary: This paper proposes a dynamic squeezing technique, called Hamiltonian Amplification, to significantly boost the phase sensitivity of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. By strategically applying squeezing operations, the protocol achieves sensitivity enhancements surpassing the standard quantum limit and even the Heisenberg limit. Crucially, the method is shown to maintain high performance even when accounting for realistic photon losses.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of enhancing the phase sensitivity of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) beyond the standard quantum limit and potentially beyond the Heisenberg limit.
main_result: A dynamic squeezing protocol, implemented via Hamiltonian Amplification (HA), was shown to enhance phase sensitivity generically, achieving super-Heisenberg scaling even with vacuum input and remaining robust against moderate photon loss.
method: The enhancement is achieved by applying alternating squeezing operations within the MZI structure, modeled using a Trotterized sequence of unitary operations.

key_observables: Phase uncertainty ($\Delta\phi$), minimum phase uncertainty ($\Delta\phi_{\min}$), and the enhancement factor ($\lambda$).
important_parameters: Squeezing strength ($r$), number of Trotter steps ($N$), and the effective loss parameter ($l_{	ext{eff}}$).

figures_summary: Figures illustrate the minimum phase uncertainty versus the number of Trotter steps ($N$) for various input states, comparing the HA protocol against the Standard Quantum Limit (SQL). Other figures show robustness against varying levels of photon loss.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the HA protocol using squeezing sequences, deriving the enhancement factor in the Trotter limit. It then compares the resulting phase sensitivity for coherent, vacuum, and squeezed vacuum inputs relative to the SQL and HL. Finally, it extends the analysis to include realistic photon loss models.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, implementable quantum sensing protocol that surpasses fundamental quantum limits, which is highly relevant for quantum optics and quantum metrology.
